claim: Carrières des Lumières 2026 hours are seasonal: Jan/Nov/Dec 10am–6pm; Feb/Mar 9:30am–6pm; Apr–Jun & Sep/Oct 9:30am–7pm; Jul/Aug 9am–7:30pm; last admission one hour before closing.
quote: January, November, December: 10am–6pm. February & March: 9:30am–6pm. April, May, June, September, October: 9:30am–7pm. July & August: 9am–7:30pm. Last admission occurs one hour before closing.

claim: The 2026 Carrières des Lumières program is Picasso 'L'art en mouvement' (40-min long programme, 450+ images covering painting, drawing, engraving, sculpture, ceramics, collage) plus a short Frida Kahlo programme 'En plein cœur' (14 min), opening 13 February 2026.
quote: Du 13 février 2026… plus de 450 images d'œuvres, de photographies et d'archives… 'Picasso, l'art en mouvement'… accompagnée d'un programme court dédié à Frida Kahlo… 'Frida Kahlo, en plein cœur'… 14 minutes.

claim: Château des Baux is open every day all year (closed 25 December); 2026 seasonal hours: Jan/Feb/Nov/Dec 10am–5pm; Mar/Oct 9:30am–6pm; Apr/May/Jun/Sep 9am–7pm; Jul/Aug 9am–7:30pm.
quote: Ouvert tous les jours toute l'année — Open everyday all year round. January, February, November and December: 10.00 am to 5.00 pm; March, October: 9.30 am to 6.00 pm; April, May, June, September: 9.00 am to 7.00 pm; July, August: 9.00 am to 7.30 pm.

claim: Château des Baux 2026 admission: adult €10, senior €9, child 7–17 €7, family (2+2) €27, under-7 free; the site spans 7 hectares with reconstructed medieval siege engines (trebuchet, ballista) on the plateau.
quote: Adults: 10€; Seniors (over 65): 9€; Children (under 7): free; Children 7 to 17 years: 7€; Family (2 adults + 2 children aged 7 to 17): 27€.

claim: The Château hosts the largest collection of full-scale reconstructed medieval siege machines in Europe (trebuchet, ballista, battering ram, couillard), with live firing demonstrations using real projectiles in season from costumed staff.
quote: Catapult demonstrations typically occur at 11:00 am, 3:30 pm, and 5:30 pm daily… reconstructions of medieval siege engines such as catapults and trebuchets… shooting demonstrations every day using real projectiles.

claim: The Carrières quarry was repurposed as 'Cathédrale d'Images' by Albert Plécy in 1975 with the first audiovisual show on Easter Monday 1977; after his death and Anne Plécy's death in 2002, the city handed management to Culturespaces in 2008 and the site reopened in 2012 as Carrières de Lumières.
quote: Albert Plécy established the 'Cathedral of Images' in the white limestone quarries of Les Baux-de-Provence in 1975… The first performance took place on Easter Monday 1977… In 2008, the city… entrust management to Culturespaces, and the site reopened in 2012 under the name Carrières de Lumières.

claim: The Pavillon de la Reine Jeanne is a hexagonal Renaissance corner-pavilion built ~1568–1581 for Jeanne de Quiqueran in the Vallon de la Fontaine below the village; Frédéric Mistral had a replica built for his tomb in Maillane.
quote: Renaissance style built for Jeanne de Quiqueran… nestled in the Vallon de la Fontaine near the old washhouse… hexagonal plan… Frédéric Mistral had a replica built for his tomb in Maillane.

claim: The 12th–16th century Église Saint-Vincent is partly carved into the rock and contains the de Manville flamboyant Gothic funerary chapel and modern stained-glass windows by Max Ingrand, donated by Prince Rainier III of Monaco.
quote: Built between the 12th and 16th centuries, the Church of Saint-Vincent is partly carved out of the rock… funerary chapel of the de Manville family, with its flamboyant Gothic vault, and Max Ingrand's modern stained-glass windows, donated… by Prince Rainier III of Monaco.

claim: L'Oustau de Baumanière is roughly 0.1 mi (≈200 m) from Carrières des Lumières — under a 5-minute walk — and the quarry sits under 10 minutes' walk from the village core.
quote: L'Oustau de Baumaniere is 0.1 mi from Carrières des Lumières… Carrières are less than 10 minutes walk from the village of Les Baux-de-Provence.

claim: Les Baux's main street is dense with lavender-soaped souvenir shops and overpriced snacks; the consensus workaround is to arrive early morning or stay into late afternoon after the day-trippers leave, or visit off-season (Sep–Oct).
quote: Les Baux is incredibly touristy and filled with shop after shop… overpriced, from souvenirs to snacks to meals… Stay late in the day, after the tour buses leave; spend the night… or come off-season.

claim: Practical visitor advice: village is fully pedestrian with multiple paid lots at the base that fill even in winter; arrive in the morning for parking and cooler air, return for late-afternoon light when buses depart; allow a half-day for château + village + Carrières.
quote: Multiple paid lots accommodate cars and campers around the village base… in high summer it is best to arrive early in the day… linger into late afternoon to enjoy better light once day-trippers depart.

claim: Van Gogh was institutionalized at Saint-Paul-de-Mausole from 8 May 1889 to 16 May 1890; visitors today see the cloister, chapel, Roman promenades, and a reconstructed Van Gogh bedroom.
quote: 8 mai 1889 au 16 mai 1890 ... la chambre de Van Gogh ... le cloître et les chemins botaniques, chapelle et clocher, promenades romaines, galerie Valetudo

claim: During his 53-week stay Van Gogh produced 143 oil paintings and over 100 drawings including The Starry Night, Irises, Olive Orchard, and Wheat Field with Cypresses; the monastery still functions as a psychiatric institution and houses an active art-therapy studio.
quote: he carried out 143 oil paintings and more than 100 drawings in the space of 53 weeks ... The Irises, Starry Night, Olive Orchard, Wheat field with Cypress, and Garden in the St-Paul hospice

claim: Saint-Paul-de-Mausole is open daily from 9 Feb 2026 through 3 Jan 2027; winter hours 10:15-12 and 13-17:15 (last entry 16:30), summer hours from 1 April 9:30-19:00 (last entry 18:30); 2026 entry fee €10.
quote: From February 9, 2026 until January 3, 2027 ... From February 8 to March 31: 10:15 AM to 12 PM and 1 PM to 5:15 PM ... From April 1 onwards: 9:30 AM to 7 PM ... EUR 10

claim: Glanum is a Greco-Roman city (capital of the Glaniques, flourished under Rome until ~270 AD) with columned villas, forum, thermal baths and mosaics; full-price entry €9, audioguide €3; April-September open daily 9:30-18:00.
quote: Glanum is an ancient archaeological site ... Full price: €9.00 ... April 1–September 30: 9:30 AM–6 PM ... last admission 45 minutes before closing

claim: Les Antiques — the Mausoleum of the Julii (30-20 BC) and the Triumphal Arch (the oldest in France, Augustan era) — stand on an open esplanade about 1 km south of town and are freely accessible at any time of day, classified national monuments since 1840.
quote: the Mausoleum and the oldest triumphal arch in France ... classified as national monuments in 1840 ... freely accessible at any time of day. Les Antiques never closes

claim: The Saint-Rémy Provençal market runs every Wednesday 8:00-13:00 year-round on Place de la République and through the historic centre, with hundreds of stalls of herbs, olives, oils, produce, honey, flowers, linens, lavender and crafts.
quote: every Wednesday between 8 am and 1 pm ... Place de la République and in the streets of the historic centre ... herbs, spices, olives, oils, fruits, vegetables, honeys, flowers

claim: A smaller Saturday morning market also runs 8-13; the pedestrianised old town offers art galleries, cafés and ice-cream parlours and a day is enough to cover the main sights.
quote: Market days in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence are on Wednesday and Saturday, from 8am to 1pm ... you likely only need a day in St. Rémy de Provence

claim: Nostradamus (Michel de Nostredame) was born in 1503 at 6 rue Hoche in the old town; a fountain at the corner of rue Carnot and rue Nostradamus and a zodiac fresco on Boulevard Mirabeau commemorate him.
quote: born in 1503 in the family home at 6 rue Hoche ... fountain dedicated to Nostradamus at the corner of rue Carnot and rue Nostradamus ... colourful fresco of Nostradamus and a zodiac

claim: Musée Estrine occupies an 18th-century Provençal hôtel particulier in the old town and houses the Van Gogh Interpretation Centre; the experience is interpretive (panels and a lyrical French-language film) rather than original-painting-heavy, with a 20th/21st-century collection of 1000+ works.
quote: former 18th century mansion ... interpretive rather than object-heavy, with display panels and a lyrical film (in French) ... more than 1000 works

claim: Free parking lots ring the old town (Boulevard Marceau, Place de la République, Avenue Frédéric Mistral, Parking de la Libération); on Wednesday market days arrive before 9 a.m. or use the free shuttle from the Petite Crau car park (every 15 min, 9:00-13:00).
quote: main parking lot is on Boulevard Marceau ... Parking de la Libération ... arrive before 9 a.m. ... free shuttle bus service from the Petite Crau car park between 9am and 1pm, running every 15 minutes

claim: Spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October) are the best seasons — pleasant temperatures, strong Provençal light, fewer crowds; Wednesday morning is the recommended day to catch the full market atmosphere.
quote: Spring (April-May) and autumn (September-October) offer the best conditions: pleasant temperatures, magnificent light and fewer tourists ... Wednesday mornings are recommended to coincide with market day

claim: Arles' Roman and Romanesque monuments are inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1981), with the city second only to Rome in number of Roman remains preserved.
quote: Arles is a good example of the adaptation of an ancient city to medieval European civilization. It has some impressive Roman monuments, of which the earliest – the arena, the Roman theatre and the cryptoporticus (subterranean galleries) – date back to the 1st century B.C.

claim: The Arles Amphitheatre (Arènes) was built around 90 AD, seats up to 21,000, and in 2026 opens daily 9am–7pm (May–Sept) with €11 adult admission.
quote: Opening hours for 2026: May 1 to September 30 daily between 9 am and 7 pm; October 1-31 daily between 9 am and 6 pm; November 2 2026 to February 28 2027 daily between 10:30 am and 4:30 pm. Admission: €11 full price, €9 reduced.

claim: Frank Gehry's LUMA Arles Tower, panoramic terraces, Carsten Höller slides and the landscaped park/skatepark are free to access; only the exhibition galleries require a paid ticket, and admission is exceptionally free 1–30 April 2026.
quote: From April 1 to April 30, 2026, admission to LUMA Arles is exceptionally free and no ticket is required... The entrance to The Tower designed by Frank Gehry, the panoramic terraces, the slides created by artist Carsten Höller, as well as all artistic installations within The Tower are freely accessible.

claim: The Pass Liberté (€13–€15 adult, valid 1 month) bundles 4 monuments of choice (Amphitheatre, Théâtre Antique, Cloître Saint-Trophime, Cryptoportiques, Alyscamps, Thermes de Constantin) plus Musée Réattu and one more museum (Museon Arlaten / MDAA / Camargue), with a reduced rate at the Fondation Van Gogh.
quote: The Pass Liberté is valid for 1 month and gives you access to a choice of 4 monuments... + the Musée Réattu + a second museum of your choice... This pass also entitles you to a reduced rate for visits to the Vincent van Gogh Foundation in Arles.

claim: Fondation Vincent van Gogh Arles reopens 22 May 2026 with 'SUSPECTS — Van Gogh, Tricksters & Co.', running 22 May–18 October 2026, daily 10am–6pm (closed 27 April–21 May for changeover).
quote: SUSPECTS — VAN GOGH, TRICKSTERS & CO. ... The Foundation is closed from April 27 to May 21. We will reopen on Friday 22 May with an exhibition devoted to artists who, following Vincent van Gogh, have chosen dissidence over conformity and excess over restraint.

claim: Arles' Saturday open-air market runs along Boulevards des Lices and Clémenceau, 08:00–12:45, with roughly 450 vendors across about two kilometres — one of the largest in Provence.
quote: Open Air Market every Saturday morning on the Boulevards des Lices and Clémenceau in Arles... Saturday from 08:00 to 12:45.

claim: The Musée Départemental Arles Antique ('le musée bleu') displays the Arles-Rhône 3 — a 31-metre 1st-century Gallo-Roman flat-bottomed barge raised from the Rhône in 2011 — alongside major mosaics and the Arles bust of Julius Caesar.
quote: The Arles-Rhône 3 boat, a Gallo-Roman flat-bottomed barge raised from the Rhône in 2011, is the centerpiece of the permanent collection alongside mosaics, sculptures and the famous bust of Julius Caesar.

claim: Les Alyscamps is a Roman necropolis used for nearly 1,500 years; Van Gogh and Gauguin painted there side-by-side in late October 1888 (Van Gogh producing four canvases, Gauguin two).
quote: Vincent van Gogh and Paul Gauguin both painted The Alyscamps in 1888... van Gogh painted four canvases and Gauguin two during the period when they worked together at Arles.

claim: Espace Van Gogh — the former 16th-century Hôtel-Dieu where Van Gogh was treated after the December 1888 ear incident — has its courtyard garden restored to match his painting 'Le Jardin de la Maison de Santé'; entry is free.
quote: The 'Espace Van Gogh' is the former Hôtel-Dieu hospital where Van Gogh was treated after his ear-cutting episode. The inner garden has been faithfully restored to match the painting Vincent did of it... Free admission.

claim: Les Rencontres d'Arles 2026 — the world's largest photography festival — runs 6 July to 4 October 2026, with Opening Week 6–12 July taking over heritage sites across the city.
quote: Les Rencontres d'Arles 2026... from July 6 to October 4, 2026. Opening Week from July 6 to 12, 2026.

claim: The Théâtre Antique d'Arles, built around 12 BC under Augustus, originally seated ~10,000 and today retains two surviving columns of its scenae frons; admission €9 adult, open daily 9am–7pm in summer.
quote: Constructed during the reign of Emperor Augustus around 12 BCE... originally accommodated approximately 10,000 spectators... Standard adult tickets are around €9, with reduced rates.

claim: For day-trippers the best parking is the 500-space covered Parking du Centre (rue Émile Fassin, 24/7) or Parking des Lices; Parking Lamartine is closest to the Old Town but often full on Saturday market days.
quote: When visiting the historic center, it is best to park in the Parking des Lices or Parc du Centre, a covered car park with 500 spaces, accessible from rue Emile Fassin... Lamartine parking lot right by the northern entrance to the Old Town, though it's often full on busy market days.

claim: The Cryptoportiques are a 1st-century BC U-shaped underground Roman gallery that served as the foundation of the forum; entry €5, open 9am–7pm May–September.
quote: Built in the 1st century BC, these subterranean galleries served as the foundations of the Roman forum of Arles. The U-shaped gallery extends about 90 metres. Open 9am to 7pm May to September, admission €5.

claim: The Mont Gaussier loop from Saint-Paul de Mausole is ~8 km, 3h, 422 m gain, partially marked GR6 blue blazes, with metal ladders and secured passages near the summit (306 m).
quote: Via the plateau de la Caume it goes in the direction of the famous Rocher des Deux Trous, and the next goal is Mont Gaussier that you reach via metal ladders and some secured passages.

claim: AllTrails' Rocher des Deux Trous loop from Saint-Rémy is 4.4 mi / ~849 ft gain, moderate, 2–2.5 hours, combining Mont Gaussier, the Rock and Lac du Peirou.
quote: covers 4.4 mi, with an elevation gain of 849 ft, taking about 2–2.5 hours to complete… passes by three essential stages: Mont Gaussier, the Rocher des Deux Trous, and Lake Peirou.

claim: The Plateau de la Caume reaches 387 m and offers panorama north over the Montagnette, the Gard and Mont Ventoux, south to the Mediterranean on clear days.
quote: Rocher des Deux Trous (307m) et Plateau de la Caume (387m)… vast panoramas on both sides of the Alpilles… to the Mediterranean Sea and to the north over the Montagnette, the Gard and Mont Ventoux.

claim: The Val d'Enfer circuit at Les Baux is ~6.2 km / 2h30 with panoramic ridge views, passing eroded limestone forms once thought to inspire Dante's Hell.
quote: approximately 6.2 kilometers representing an average of 2h30 of walking… following the ridges along a wide forest path with panoramic views of the Alpilles.

claim: Access to the Alpilles massif is regulated by prefectural decree from 1 June to 30 September; the daily map is published at 6 pm for the next day with a simple green = open, red = closed scheme.
quote: Du 1er juin au 30 septembre… à 18 heures pour le lendemain.

claim: The Bouches-du-Rhône prefecture publishes an interactive massif-access map covering 25 forest massifs including the Alpilles; status is set under a prefectural arrêté.
quote: Accès au massif autorisé… Accès au massif interdit… Arrêté préfectoral.

claim: The official Alpilles climbing topo lists 1,792 routes across 13 sites in 7 communes including Mouriès, Orgon, Saint-Rémy-de-Provence and Paradou.
quote: 1792 routes spread across 13 sites and 7 communes (Aureille, Eyguières, Mouriès, Orgon, Paradou, Saint Rémy de Provence, and Tarascon).

claim: Mouriès is the headline Alpilles sport-climbing crag with 200+ routes graded 5 to 8b+ on technical limestone slabs (south face) and fingery vertical/overhanging walls (north face), up to 35 m.
quote: more than 200 routes from 5s to 8s. The South face is all about fingery super technical slabs while the North face is on a slightly overhanging/vertical (fingery) wall.

claim: The Vallon de Valample crag in Saint-Rémy offers about fifty well-equipped sport routes across three sectors of varied orientation.
quote: A good fifty well-equipped routes, with difficulty levels for everyone, are distributed across three distinct sectors with multiple orientations.

claim: Sun-e-Bike opened the first e-bike rental shop in the Alpilles at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence in 2013 and supplies e-bikes (Gazelle Medeo T9, Kalkhoff Endeavour 3) for self-guided Alpilles loops.
quote: Their Saint-Rémy-de-Provence shop, established in 2013, was the first e-bike rental company in the Alpilles.

claim: Télécycles in Maussane-les-Alpilles rents bikes with free pre-loaded 30–50 km route suggestions, lock, repair kit and front bag included.
quote: Télécycles offers free routes of 30 to 50 km with bike rental, and all bikes are delivered with a small front bag, a lock, and a repair kit.

claim: Gravel and road loops from Maussane include a 49 km circuit linking Les Baux, Maussane and Eygalières through vineyards and olive groves.
quote: Specific route options include a 49km route through Baux de Provence, Maussane-les-Alpilles and Eygalières.

claim: Chev'Alpilles, on the heights of Saint-Rémy close to Les Baux, runs 1–2 hour guided rides (€40–60) for beginners and experienced riders through the Parc Naturel Régional des Alpilles.
quote: Chev'Alpilles is located on the heights of Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, close to the picturesque village of Les Baux-de-Provence… prices of 40 to 60 € for 1-2 hour rides.

claim: Le Petit Roman runs year-round equestrian rides in the Alpilles park, including 2-hour outings over ridges and to Lac du Peirou.
quote: 2-hour tours go over the splendid ridges and along the shores of Lac du Peiroou.

claim: Provençal lavender peaks from late June through the second week of July, with the famous Valensole plateau (well outside 30 km of Les Baux) reaching full bloom in early July.
quote: peak viewing conditions occurring during the final week of June through the second week of July… The Valensole Plateau reaches full bloom in the first two weeks of July.

claim: Working lavender (and lavandin) parcels exist within the Alpilles plain itself — e.g. Château de la Gabelle's organic fields at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence — providing nearby photo spots without driving to Valensole.
quote: Nos lavandes à Saint Rémy de Provence | Producteur Bio en Provence.

claim: Hiking guidance for Provence warns against starting walks during a mistral episode because of risks of being blown off-balance and of debris in the eyes, and stresses checking the daily fire-access bulletin.
quote: Hiking guides often advise against outings during the Mistral should you be blown so violently that you lose your balance… wearing sunglasses is recommended to protect your eyes from the scattering dust and debris.

claim: The mistral is a strong, cold northwesterly wind averaging 50 km/h and gusting to 100 km/h that can blow in any season and lasts several days at a time.
quote: producing sustained winds averaging 50 km/h (30 mph), sometimes reaching 100 km/h (60 mph). It can last for several days.

claim: Moulin Castelas in Les Baux offers free mill visits and tastings year-round with no reservation, weekdays 8:30am-6:30pm and weekends 10am-1pm / 2:30pm-6:30pm.
quote: Visit of the mill and olive oil tastings are free and available all year round. Neither tours nor tastings require a reservation – just come on by!

claim: Moulin Jean-Marie Cornille is the historic cooperative oil mill in Maussane-les-Alpilles producing AOP Vallée des Baux-de-Provence olive oil.
quote: Moulin Cornille - Huile d'olives AOP de la Vallée des Baux de Provence

claim: At Moulin Cornille self-guided tours run Mon–Fri 9:30-11:45 and 13:30-16:30 for €4; guided tours by appointment at €6.50; shop open Mon-Fri 9:30-12:30 and 13:30-18:00, Sat until 18:00.
quote: Self-guided tours from Monday to Friday from 9.30am – 11.45am and 1:30 p.m. – 4:30 p.m. for €4 (free for children under 10... Guided tours by appointment Monday to Friday at 10:30 a.m. or 2:00 p.m. for €6.50

claim: The AOP Vallée des Baux-de-Provence blends at least two of four olive varieties — Salonenque (sweet, creamy), Aglandau (spicy), Grossane (grapefruit aromas), Verdale (herbaceous, green apple) — with Picholine as a complement, and counts 16 mills in the appellation area.
quote: Salonenque... gives the oil a sweet, fruity and creamy character... Aglandau... gives the oil its ardency... Grossane... grapefruit aromas... Verdale... herbaceous and green apple aromas... 16 in the appellation area.

claim: Moulin du Calanquet near Saint-Rémy, a family mill founded in 2000 by Anne and Gilles Brun, offers guided tours through olive grove and mill plus tastings of monovarietal oils, tapenades and jams, in French or English.
quote: At the end of the tour, visitors enjoy a tasting of various olive oils produced at the mill, and can sample tapenades, jams, and olives from tasting stations.

claim: From the 2023 vintage, AOP Les Baux-de-Provence became the first French wine appellation to require 100% organic viticulture across all producers.
quote: From the 2023 vintage, the AOP Les Baux-de-Provence will be the first 100% organic wine appellation.

claim: Château Romanin near Saint-Rémy offers a 1-hour guided tour with tasting at €20/person and a 2-hour prestige version at €80, showcasing biodynamic vines and its 'Cathedral Cellar' carved into the Alpilles rock by architect Serge Hennemann in 1992.
quote: A 1-hour guided tour and tasting costs €20 per person, while a 2-hour prestige tour with tasting is €80 per person.

claim: Mas de la Dame, at the foot of Les Baux, is run by Caroline Missoffe and Anne Poniatowski over 58 ha of vines and 28 ha of olives — certified organic since 1999 and now biodynamic — with tastings by reservation of wines, olive oil and tapenade.
quote: Mas de la Dame... 58 hectares of vines and 28 hectares of olive trees... private wine tastings are organized upon reservation

claim: Domaine Hauvette in Saint-Rémy, founded 1988 by Dominique Hauvette (named Vigneronne de l'année 2020 by Revue du Vin de France), farms ~17 ha biodynamically since 2003 with vinification in concrete eggs without sulfur.
quote: Today, she cultivates approximately 17 hectares, primarily in biodynamic farming since 2003... aging is done systematically in concrete eggs which accentuate the minerality

claim: Domaine de Trévallon was declassified to Vin de Pays (now IGP Alpilles) in 1993 when the new AOC Les Baux capped Cabernet Sauvignon at 20%, because Eloi Dürrbach's signature blend is 50/50 Cabernet Sauvignon / Syrah.
quote: At the time of the creation of AOC Baux de Provence in 1993, the Vineyard was degraded to Vin de Pays: too many Cabernet Sauvignon, limited to 20% of the blend in the new appellation!

claim: Mas de Gourgonnier near Mouriès, run by the Cartier family with 38 ha of vines and 18 ha of olives, was one of France's first certified organic wineries in the 1970s.
quote: Mas de Gourgonnier, with 38 hectares of grapevines and 18 hectares of olive groves... In the 1970s, this family estate was one of the first officially certified organic wineries.

claim: Mouriès' weekly Provençal market is held Wednesday mornings 8am-12:30pm on Cours Paul Révoil (temporarily relocated to Parc du Moulin Peyre from 1 October 2025 until end of March 2026 for roadworks).
quote: Due to construction work on Cours Paul Révoil, the weekly market will be temporarily relocated to Parc du Moulin Peyre from Wednesday, 1 October 2025 until the end of March 2026.

claim: The Maussane-les-Alpilles Provençal market takes place every Thursday morning 8am-1pm on Place Henri Giraud, featuring tapenade, cracked olives, goat cheeses and crafts.
quote: The Maussane-les-Alpilles market takes place on Place Henri Giraud every Thursday from 8am to 1pm.

claim: The Saint-Rémy-de-Provence market is held every Wednesday year-round 8am-1pm across Place de la République, Boulevard Marceau, Boulevard Gambetta and surrounding streets, with a free shuttle from the Petite Crau car park every 15 min.
quote: The market is held all year round on Wednesday between 8 am and 1 pm... free shuttle bus service from the Petite Crau car park between 9am and 1pm, running every 15 minutes.

claim: Maillane holds a Thursday morning market on avenue Auguste Daillan (Place de l'Église) from ~8am to 12:30pm.
quote: Le marché de Maillane se tient régulièrement le jeudi... à partir de 8 h... les vendeurs commencent à plier bagage à partir de 12 h 30.

claim: Eyguières has two weekly markets — Tuesday morning (Rue des Frères Perret / Place Monier, ~20 stalls, 8am-1pm) and Saturday morning (Place Thiers, ~25 selected vendors, 8am-12:30pm).
quote: le marché du mardi offre une grande variété de produits... le samedi met à l'honneur des vendeurs sélectionnés pour la qualité de leurs produits

claim: Château de Tarascon is a 15c riverside fortress built between 1400 and 1435 by Louis II and Louis III of Anjou, counts of Provence, with 30+ rooms and a panoramic Rhône terrace; closed Mondays.
quote: The Château of Tarascon is a fortress built by the princes of Anjou on the banks of the Rhône at the start of the 15th century... Construction took place between 1400 and 1435 under Louis II and his son Louis III, dukes of Anjou, counts of Provence.

claim: Château du Roi René opens daily April–August 9am–7pm, September–March 10:30am–5pm, closed Mondays, adult admission €6.50.
quote: open every day from April 1st to August 31st from 9 A.M. to 7 P.M., and from September 1st to March 31st from 10:30 A.M. to 5 P.M., closed on Mondays, with adult admission at 6.5 Euros

claim: The Moulin de Daudet inspired Alphonse Daudet's writings (he never owned it), is a classified historic monument since 1931, and sits on a belvedere overlooking the Rhône valley.
quote: Daudet's mill, though Alphonse Daudet never owned the mill but drew inspiration from it in his writings. The Daudet mill has been classified as a historical monument since 1931

claim: Barbegal Roman flour-mill complex near Fontvieille used 16 waterwheels fed by two aqueducts and is called 'the greatest known concentration of mechanical power in the ancient world'; the site is freely accessible.
quote: a flour mill complex powered by 16 waterwheels, fed by two aqueducts bringing water to Arles, and was considered 'the greatest known concentration of mechanical power in the ancient world'

claim: Abbaye de Montmajour 2026 hours: April–May & October–March 10am–5pm, June–September 9am–6:15pm; closed Mondays in winter; adult ticket €7, last entry 1 hour before close.
quote: April 1 - May 31: 10am - 5pm; June 1 - September 30: 9am - 6:15pm; October 1 - March 31: 10am - 5pm. Closed Mondays during the October-March period. Individual admission: €7

claim: Van Gogh produced numerous drawings of Montmajour Abbey in 1888–1889, making it a notable stop on the Van Gogh route from Arles.
quote: The site particularly fascinated Van Gogh (1853-1890), who made numerous drawings there in 1888-1889.

claim: Palais des Papes in Avignon is open daily year-round; March 1–November 1 9am–7pm; visit takes ~1.5–2 hours; tickets €12 (palace), €17 with Pont d'Avignon and gardens.
quote: March 1 – November 1: 9am–7pm... Palace only: €12... Palace + Avignon Bridge + Gardens: €17... Visite du Palais des Papes : environ 1h30 – 2h

claim: Official Les Baux tourism site lists drive times of 20 km/30 min to Arles and 35 km/40 min to Avignon (so Avignon is at the practical edge of a half-day from Les Baux).
quote: Arles: 20 km (30 min); Avignon: 35 km (40 min)

claim: Abbey of Saint-Gilles is UNESCO-listed (as part of the Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France) and famed for its 1120–1160 Romanesque carved façade with three portals depicting Old/New Testament scenes.
quote: included in the UNESCO Heritage List as part of the World Heritage Sites of the Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France... The façade was built from 1120 to 1160 and features a decorated entrance portico with three portals

claim: Beaucaire Fortress is a free-to-visit 11c Counts-of-Toulouse stronghold facing Tarascon across the Rhône, with seasonal hours and rampart views; July–August daily 9:30am–8pm.
quote: The vestiges of this château médiéval can be visited free of charge all year... July 1 to August 31, 2026: Daily 09:30-20:00

claim: Les Baux village requires parking outside the walls; all lots are paid year-round 8am–7pm at €5 for the first hour, with no free parking and a €35 illegal-parking fine.
quote: All parking areas are paid year-round from 8am to 7pm at €5 for the first hour... There are no free parking spaces in Les Baux-de-Provence... Illegal parking is prohibited and subject to a €35 fine.

claim: In France most non-food shops close Sundays; bakeries/butchers/patisseries can open until 13:00, cafés and restaurants can open all day, and a business open Sunday often closes Monday instead.
quote: Businesses selling food such as bakeries, cheese shops, butchers, patisseries, and fishmongers are allowed to open until 13:00 on Sundays. Cafes and restaurants can open all day on Sunday... if a store or restaurant is open on Sunday, they might actually close on Monday instead.

claim: A standard 2–3 day Alpilles loop pairs Arles + Les Baux + Saint-Rémy by car since all are within easy reach, and Saint-Rémy is ~20 min from Les Baux.
quote: Arles, Les Baux de Provence and St Remy de Provence are all within easy reach of each other by car... Saint Rémy-de-Provence: 20 min, Arles: 30-40 min, Avignon: 40-50 min from Les Baux.
